title: AOSP Repo, Sync, Build, and Source-tree Navigation Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies aosp repo, sync, build, and source-tree navigation?
options: Pin the manifest and target, respect Repo project ownership, build narrowly then integratively, and record exact environment and artifacts.
Treat tree as one Git repo
questions.answer: Pin the manifest and target, respect Repo project ownership, build narrowly then integratively, and record exact environment and artifacts.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: The AOSP source tree is a single Git repository whose subdirectories share one branch and commit.
questions.explanation: Editing files across several Git projects on one ordinary branch misses Repo project boundaries and makes upload or review incomplete.

questions.prompt: What does a Repo manifest determine?
questions.answer: Which Git projects, revisions, remotes, paths, and groups compose the checked-out AOSP workspace.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
